{{Short description|American physicist}}
'''David R. Smith''' is an American  [[physicist]] and [[professor]] of [[electrical engineering|electrical]] and [[computer engineering]] at [[Duke University]] in [[North Carolina]] and visiting professor at [[Imperial College London]].<ref>{{Cite web
| last =  | first =  | title = Duke University, Electrical and Computer Engineering, David R. Smith| url = https://ece.duke.edu/people/david-smith/ | publisher =  | date= | access-date = 2024-09-24
}}</ref> Smith's research focuses on [[Electromagnetic spectrum|electromagnetic]] [[metamaterial]]s, or materials with a [[Negative refractive index#Negative refractive index|negative index of refraction]].

Smith obtained his [[B.Sc.]] and [[Ph.D.]] in physics from the [[University of California, San Diego]] (UCSD) in 1988 and 1994. In 2000, as a postdoctoral fellow working in the laboratory of Professor [[Sheldon Schultz]] at UCSD, Smith and his colleagues discovered the first material that exhibited a negative [[index of refraction]].<ref>{{Citation
 | title = Experimental verification of a negative index of refraction
 | jstor = 3082888
 | year = 2001
 | journal = Science
 | pages = 77–79
 | volume = 292
 | issue = 5514
 | last1 = Shelby| first1 =  R. A.
 | last2 =  Smith| first2 =  D. R.
 | last3 =  Schultz| first3 =  S.|bibcode = 2001Sci...292...77S |doi = 10.1126/science.1058847 | pmid=11292865| s2cid = 9321456
 }}</ref><ref name=Pendry2004>{{cite journal|last =Pendry|first =John B.|author-link =John Pendry|title =Negative Refraction|journal =Contemporary Physics|volume =45|issue =3|pages =191–202|year =2004|doi =10.1080/00107510410001667434|bibcode =2004ConPh..45..191P|s2cid =218544892|doi-access =free}}</ref>

For his research in metamaterials, Smith, along with four European researchers, was awarded the [[Descartes Prize]] in 2005, the [[European Union]]'s top prize for collaborative research.<ref name="www.physorg.com">{{Cite web
| last =  | first =  | title = David R. Smith Shares Descartes Award for Material that Reverses Lights Properties | url = http://www.physorg.com/news8688.html | publisher =  | date= 2005-12-02| access-date = 2009-10-16
}}</ref> He is known also as the first person to create a functioning [[cloak of invisibility]] that renders an object invisible in microwave wavelengths.<ref>{{cite news
| first=Fred | last=Hapgood | title=Metamaterial Revolution: The New Science of Making Anything Disappear | date= 2009-03-10 | url= http://discovermagazine.com/2009/apr/10-metamaterial-revolution-new-science-making-anything-disappear/article_view?b_start:int=2 | access-date = 2009-10-10
}}</ref><ref name=Silverman>{{Citation 
| title = HowStuffWorks: Is it possible to make a cloaking device? | url = http://science.howstuffworks.com/cloaking-device.htm/printable | author = Silverman, Jacob | access-date = 2009-10-16 
| date = 2007-06-25 }}</ref><ref name="www.sciencedaily.com">{{Cite web 
| last =  | first =  | title = Theoretical Blueprint For Invisibility Cloak Reported | url = https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2006/05/060525193729.htm | publisher =  | date = 2006-05-25 | access-date = 2009-10-16
}}</ref> Although the cloaking device had limited ability to conceal an object from light of a single microwave wavelength, the experiment was an initial demonstration of the potential of metamaterials, constructed composite materials with unusual optical properties, to behave in unique ways because of both their structural properties.<ref name=Silverman />

In 2009, [[Reuters]] news service listed Smith in the [[List of Clarivate Citation laureates in Physics|Clarivate Citation laureates in Physics]], which considers potential candidates for the [[Nobel Prize in Physics]].<ref>{{cite web
| url= https://www.reuters.com/article/pressRelease/idUS37530+24-Sep-2009+PRN20090924
| archive-url= https://archive.today/20120913213121/http://www.reuters.com/article/pressRelease/idUS37530+24-Sep-2009+PRN20090924
| archive-date= 2012-09-13
| title= Thomson Reuters Predicts Nobel Laureates
| website= [[Reuters]]
| date= 2009-09-24
}}</ref>
